hints: Use the given downhill motion to find the friction force. Then remember friction reverses when the body goes up.
worded:
1. Sliding down: 2 × 10 × ½ − f = 2 × 3, so f = 4 N.

2. Going up at 3 m/s²: F must beat gravity’s 10 N and friction’s 4 N (now down the slope) and supply 6 N: F = 20 N. (B)

3. Check: kinetic friction μmg cos 30° = 4 N gives μ ≈ 0.23, the same both ways, since N does not change when the motion reverses.
conventional:
![](asset:P000560-sol-1)

Down: $mg\sin 30^{\circ} - f = ma \Rightarrow f = 10 - 6 = 4$ N.
Up: $F - mg\sin 30^{\circ} - f = ma \Rightarrow F = 10 + 4 + 6 = 20$ N.
mistakes: Friction changes direction when the motion reverses.
